subject: Culture
title: Suffragette White
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Suffragette White.

hook.text: In 1908, suffragettes wore white to protests. Against violent police, the white made brutality impossible to ignore.

buildup.text: The suffragette movement assigned colors: white for purity, purple for dignity, and green for hope.

discovery.text: Dressing uniformly turned individual women into a visual army. The press couldn't dismiss a sea of white.

twist.text: In 2019, US congresswomen wore white to the State of the Union address—a direct callback to suffragette symbolism.

climax.text: Political clothing works because it turns the body into a protest sign that walks, sits, and can't be confiscated.

punchline.text: When you wear your cause, no one can take away your sign.

quiz.question: What did the color white symbolize for suffragettes?

details.summary: Suffragettes strategically wore white to symbolize purity and moral authority in their fight for women's voting rights. This deliberate fashion choice countered critics who portrayed them as unladylike radicals, turning clothing into a calculated political weapon.
details.whyItMatters: The suffragette use of white demonstrates how marginalized groups weaponize fashion to reframe public perception and advance political causes.
takeaways: Suffragettes used white, purple, and green as movement colors
White symbolized purity to counter accusations of radicalism
Women politicians still wear white as a suffragette tribute

faq.question: Why did suffragettes choose white, purple, and green?
faq.answer: White represented purity, purple symbolized dignity, and green stood for hope. These colors were adopted by the Women's Social and Political Union in 1908. The combination allowed supporters to show solidarity through everyday dress — a subtle but visible political statement.

faq.question: Do politicians still wear white as a suffragette reference?
faq.answer: Yes. Female US politicians, including Hillary Clinton and members of Congress, have worn white to State of the Union addresses and inaugurations as a deliberate tribute to suffragettes. Kamala Harris wore white on election night 2020 and at her inauguration.
